tweet_summary: Conservative reporter Cam Higby shares video screenshots of a PDF titled 'Patrolling/Commuting,' calling it 'the entire TRAINING MANUAL for domestic terrorist patrols chasing ICE agents in Minneapolis.' Got 6M impressions and an Elon Musk reply.
why_note_decision: The document shown in the video is the MN ICE Watch 'Patrolling/Commuting' observation guide. On its face it instructs OBSERVATION: explicitly bans weapons (even pocket/utility knives), children, pets, alcohol, and going live; tells patrollers to stay safe, document, contact dispatch and ACLU, and avoid confrontation. Calling it a manual for 'domestic terrorist patrols chasing ICE agents' is a substantive mischaracterization of the document on screen. The original (NEEDS_MORE_RATINGS) note is also wrong: it calls this document the 'De-Arrest Primer' — but the De-Arrest Primer is a SEPARATE document (NY Post 2026-01-12) authored Spring 2024 with 'micro-intifada' framing. Conflating the two documents is a factual error.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note correctly identifies the document on screen as an MN ICE Watch 'Patrolling/Commuting' OBSERVATION guide (whistles, dispatch, ACLU reporting, no weapons/children/pets) — NOT a 'de-arrest' manual and NOT a 'training manual for chasing ICE agents.' It is acceptable to mention the document explicitly bans weapons. FAIL notes that (a) repeat the 'De-Arrest Primer' mislabel from the original note (the de-arrest primer is a separate Spring-2024 document), or (b) endorse the 'domestic terrorist patrols' characterization without qualifier, or (c) ignore the on-screen content (no weapons, no children, observe-and-document).
reference_note: The document shown is MN ICE Watch's 'Patrolling/Commuting' observation guide — it explicitly bans weapons (incl. pocket knives), children, pets, and going live, and instructs observers to document, alert dispatch, and contact the ACLU. It is distinct from a separate Spring-2024 'De-Arrest Primer' MN ICE Watch reposted, which contains the 'micro-intifada' language. https://nypost.com/2026/01/12/us-news/minnesota-ice-watch-group-shared-de-arresting-manual-comparing-tactics-for-fighting-cops-to-a-micro-intifada

original_unhelpful_note.text: The document is a "De-Arrest Primer" from the Minnesota ICE Watch activist group, which provides tactics for interfering with arrests by law enforcement, including ICE, during protests. It is not a manual for "domestic terrorist patrols chasing ICE agents."  https://nypost.com/2026/01/12/us-news/minnesota-ice-watch-group-shared-de-arresting-manual-comparing-tactics-for-fighting-cops-to-a-micro-intifada
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: incorrect: misidentifies the document — the video shows the 'Patrolling/Commuting' observation guide, not the separately-published 'De-Arrest Primer' the NY Post reported on

fact_check.notes: The video clearly shows pages titled 'Patrolling/Commuting' with mobile/foot patrol observation instructions, whistles, dispatch protocol, an explicit ban on weapons/children/pets, and ACLU reporting. The separately-reported 'De-Arrest Primer' (NY Post, 2026-01-12) is a different document with 'micro-intifada' language about 'shaking off' arrests.

importance.lens_rationale: 6M impressions + Elon Musk amplification + 'domestic terrorist' framing of activists who are observing federal agents has real safety/democratic-discourse stakes; getting which-document-is-this right matters.
